subject: createRSV() has no destroy(): duplicate listeners if mission 2 mounts without a page reload
description:
Nancy, 2026-08-10, reviewing the flight-engine extraction (1d878afe1). _app/houses/cloud/games/lib/rsv-flight.js registers keydown/keyup/blur/mousemove on window plus click on renderer.domElement, and returns no teardown. Safe TODAY only because the sole restart path is a full page reload: cloud-cold-horizon.html:2029 sets againBtn.onclick = () => location.reload(), so createRSV() runs exactly once per page life.

THE LANDMINE IS AIMED AT THE EXACT USE CASE THE EXTRACTION EXISTS TO ENABLE. The moment a second flying mission (or an arena shell that mounts missions without navigating) calls createRSV() again on a live page, the listeners STACK: double-applied thrust, doubled command-queue pushes, double killRel bursts. Nothing exercises it today, so it is latent, not live. Nancy verdict was PROCEED and this did not block the deploy.

FIX: return destroy() from createRSV that removes all five listeners, and call it before any re-mount. Close this BEFORE mission 2 adopts createRSV under a non-reload flow, not after it is discovered by one.

Second, smaller: damage is destructured at cloud-cold-horizon.html:1035 but has no call site in the HTML (the module calls it internally; onDamage is the real mission hook). Dead binding, harmless, an artifact of keeping original names so downstream code stayed untouched.

Third: onKey 'h' (showCoach) and 'escape' (hideCoach) are covered by NEITHER playthrough.js NOR strand-test.js. Pre-existing gap, disclosed not hidden, confirmed by Chris via grep. Worth closing before a third mission reuses that wiring.
[2026-08-11 00:54] FIXED 2026-08-10. createRSV now returns destroy(): named handlers, removes all five listeners, clears held keys, idempotent. Covered by _tools/qa/cold-horizon/rsv-teardown-test.js 6/6, which reproduces the double-apply with two live instances BEFORE proving destroy fixes it. Deliberately not called from cloud-cold-horizon.html or lagrange-inspect.html: both are full-page missions where navigation already tears down, so a call there would be dead code that reads as load-bearing. playthrough 26/26 and acts-test 80/80 unchanged.
